FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Chemical 
Methods of Test Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 

In the preparation of this standard considerable assistance has been derived from DIN 53923 /Testing of textile — 
Determination of water absorption of textile fabrics' . 

In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed 
or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 *Rules for rounding off 
numerical values {revised)'. 



IS 14579 : 1998 



Indian Standard 



TEXTILES — METHOD FOR DETERMINATION 
OF ABSORB ANCY OF TERRY TOWELS 



1 SCOPE 

This standard prescribes a method for determination 
of water absorption of terry towels and fabrics having 
high water absorption capacity. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary adjuncts 
to this standard : 

IS No. Title 

460 (Part 2) : Specification for test sieves; Part 2 
1985 Perforated plate test sieves {third 

revision) 

6359 : 197 1 Method for conditioning of textiles 

9022: 1979 Methods for preparation of 

laboratory test samples and test 
specimens of textile materials for 
chemical testing 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

For the purpose this standard, the following definition 
shall apply. 

3.1 Water Absorption Capacity 

The water absorption capacity is the quantity of water 
absorbed by a textile material after storage in water 
and expressed as percentage of original weight of the 
material. 

4 APPARATUS 

4.1 Stainless steel perforated plate test sieve of at least 
120 mm X 120 mm with metallic frame [see IS 460 

(Part 2)]. 

4.2 Suitable vessel with distilled water for inserting 
the wire netting with the test piece placed on it. 

4.3 Glass weighing bottle with ground lid. 

5 SAMPLING AND SAMPLE PREPARATION 

Test pieces of 100 mm x 100 mm are cut out from the 
test specimens. If an individual test piece weighs lesser 



than I g, several test pieces are put one above the other 
to form a test piece stack which shall weigh at least 1 
g. At least 5 test pieces/stacks shall be tested. 

6 PROCEDURE 

The test piece and/or stack conditioned to moisture 
equilibrium in standard atmosphere in accordance 
with IS 6359 is weighed up to 0.01 g (wk). It is then 
put on the perforated plate test sieve and fixed with 
pins or clips on the corners. The sieve with the test 
piece put on it, is immersed flat in a suitable vessel 
containing distilled water at 27 ± 1 ^C in such a manner 
that the top edge of frame is at least 20 mm below the 
water level. The formation of air bubbles under the test 
piece is avoided by introducing the sieve slant in 
water, Afteranexposuretimeof 60s ±3 s, the sieve 
with the test piece is removed from the vessel and after 
removing three pins or clips it is tilted against the 
horizontal line for dripping for a period of 120 s ± 3 s 
in such a manner that the test piece is lifted off the sieve 
and allowed to hang freely. The test piece is removed 
from the sieve and is placed in a tared weighing bottle 
which is closed immediately with the lid and is 
weighed up to 0.01 g. The weight of the wet test piece 
is denoted by mn. 

7 EVALUATION 

The water absorption (Wa) in percent by weight 
referring to the weight of conditioned test piece (mk) 
is calculated as under: 

w, = hhizjuk ^ ,00 

Calculate average of five specimens tested. 

8 TEST REPORT 

The test report shall include the following: 

a) Type and description of the test pieces; 

b) Number of layers; 

c) Water absorption in percent by weight rounded 
to whole number; 

d) Individual values and arithmetic mean; and 

e) Deviations , if any, trom the standard.

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and 
attending to connected matters in the country.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on Ujje basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirn^l when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue 
of *BIS Handbook' and 'Standards Monthly Additions'
